description:
We have to use Ubuntu package manager apt-get to install MySQL server. Just run the below command and set a root password if required

apt-get -y install mysql-server

If you want to interact with server, obviously we need to install client, just type

apt-get -y install mysql-client

If you didn't see any error message,Congratulations! you have successfully installed MySQL!

Lets test your IQ with simple question :p Do you know What does the word Ubuntu mean?
name: Mysql Installation

description:
In order to configure MySQL server, we need to start the server. Lets do it
service mysql start
Now server is running lets make it secure by executing below binary
mysql_secure_installation

This will prompt you for root password. If you didn't set the root password yet , press enter Otherwise provide the root password to proceed
Enter current password for root (enter for none):
Now you will get a series of Y/n options.

Press Y to set root password.
Change the root password?

Press 'Y' to remove anonymous user
Remove anonymous users?[Y/n] Y

Press 'Y' to remove test database
Remove test database and access to it? [Y/n] Y

Next, Press Y If you want to disable remote MySQL root login.
Disallow root login remotely? [Y/n] Y

At last we need to reload the tables to so that above changes will be applied
Reload privilege tables now? [Y/n] Y
name: Configure MySQL server

description:
Now Its time to verify the installation.

Do you remember the MySQL root password? okay great!, Now connect to server mysqld via client mysql with the command :

mysql -u root -p

Welcome to the MySQL monitor.
...
...
Type 'help;' or '\h' for help. Type '\c' to clear the current input statement.
mysql>

If you see similar welcome message and mysql prompt,then everything went well :) Great! You have Installed and Configured MySQL Server under Ubuntu. Hope you enjoyed this short tutorial, See you later!
